_comment: wp_ct — the ONE certificate-transparency client. Tunables for every CT source it asks: the observation window each source can honestly claim (printed next to its status so a ~1-year mirror is never read as full history), crt.sh's retry/backoff/wall-clock budgets and PostgreSQL fallback, the keyless backups' paging, and the listing caps (a cap always records the true total + a truncated flag — never a silent cut). Budgets are WALL-CLOCK seconds for the whole step, enforced around it, not per socket read.

windows._comment: Observation window per source, shown beside its status in every collection and report. crt.sh is the only full public CT history; every backup is a partial mirror. Measured 2026-10: Shodan CTL / CertSpotter / CertIndex / CertKit hold about one year; Netlas reaches back years but sparsely; Censys answers a capped sample of its own global index (CT plus scanning).

entries.censys: capped sample of a global certificate index
entries.agniops(aggregated): names only, not CT-attributable, undisclosed provenance

crtsh._comment: crt.sh web front end: q= then identity= per attempt, backoff step x attempt capped at backoff_cap, inside web_budget_seconds for the whole sub-query; one attempt never waits longer than attempt_timeout. After the web budget is exhausted the per-process breaker stays open for breaker_cooldown_seconds so later seeds in the same run go straight to PostgreSQL instead of paying the web budget again. PostgreSQL (guest@crt.sh:5432/certwatch, no password, ~1 min/query) needs the optional psycopg package; pg_row_limit rows back means the listing was capped, not complete.

backups._comment: Keyless CT backups that run ONLY when crt.sh is degraded or empty (strict fallback). request_timeout_seconds bounds each HTTP request; certspotter_max_pages bounds the after=<id> page walk — reaching it records status `capped`, a later page failing records `partial`, the first page failing records `failed` (HTTP 429 there = `skipped-quota`).

aggregated._comment: Keyless AGGREGATED name indexes (crt.name, agniops) — CT unioned with crawl/zone/feed data, so a hit is NOT CT-log evidence and discloses the apex to a third party. Asked LAST, only when every CT source (keyed ones and Censys included) left no name at all; names land in aggregated_subdomains, never in subdomains, and never count toward completeness.

certkit._comment: CertKit Discovery (app.certkit.io) — no API, so wp_certkit logs in with CERTKIT_EMAIL / CERTKIT_PASSWORD and downloads the Discovery CSV export. ~1 year, expired included, day-only dates, real x509 serials. The session (cookies + collection id) is cached in MEMORY/certkit_session.json (0600) for session_ttl_seconds so per-host collectors do not log in once each. Breaks when MFA is on or the login form changes — reported as `failed` with the reason.

certindex._comment: CertIndex (api.ctindex.io, X-API-Key CERTINDEX_API_KEY). FREE TIER IS PERSONAL / NON-COMMERCIAL ONLY. Currently valid certificates only (~1 year). full_domain lookups are 10/hour ACCOUNT-WIDE and each page is one lookup, so wp_certindex reads the free /v1/usage first and never waits on a quota: none left → `skipped-quota`. max_pages bounds one domain's share of the hour (reaching it = `capped`). page_size above 100 drops issuer and not_after. A first query of a new domain is partial while CertIndex backfills (coverage.basis not `domain_backfill_completed…`, or total_is_lower_bound) → `partial`, asked again on a later call.

netlas._comment: Netlas certificates index (NETLAS_API_KEY, metered) — the only backup with multi-year history, asked ONLY when crt.sh is degraded (never on an authoritative empty) and never under --free-only. Query certificate.names:<d> (subject_dn misses most; names:*. and subject.common_name time out). Token matching returns look-alikes, so only <d> and *.<d> names survive the filter. A cold first download can be short: certs_count is compared and a short download is `partial`. hard_limit_seconds is enforced around the WHOLE count + download, not per socket read.

censys._comment: Censys certificate search — LAST RESORT, only when every other CT source left no certificate, never under --free-only. Spends credits through wp_censys's own budget (5 per page). Exact-match cert.names="<d>" / "*.<d>" (the tokenised `:` form matches millions of unrelated certificates; regex `=~` is rejected). A global index (CT plus Censys's own scanning), so it can hold self-signed / private-CA certificates that never reached CT. Page walk: complete / capped are final even when empty; partial (budget or a later page failed) is asked again; first-page failure is `failed`, never 'none'.

related_hosts._comment: Pivot hits — hosts sharing a certificate fingerprint, favicon or tracking ID with the target — are RELATED HOSTS (unverified), never the target's server, origin or hosting/abuse contact by themselves. Each is graded by how many origin checks agree: (1) the IP serves the target's content for Host: <target> (same body hash; an active request — `not run` unless /cert-pivot ran it live, through the egress proxy; an unreachable IP stays `not run`, never a `fail`), (2) the shared certificate is the target's own non-CDN leaf whose SANs include the target, (3) the target's own passive DNS / passive SSL / DNS history shows it on that IP, (4) the IP is outside CDN / WAF / parking / bogon ranges. rungs[n] is the label for n agreeing checks; an address that FAILS check (4) gets edge_rung whatever else agrees, because an edge serves the target's content and certificate by design. cdn_cert_issuer_markers mark a CDN-managed certificate (check 2 fails on it). max_rows bounds the rendered table (the full list stays in the JSON); probe_max_ips / probe_timeout_seconds bound /cert-pivot's Host-header probe.
related_hosts.edge_rung: edge / non-routable address (CDN, WAF, parking, bogon) — not an origin

listing._comment: How many certificates / subdomains a merged CT result lists inline. The full counts are always recorded (cert_total, subdomain_total) with a truncated flag, so a capped listing is never read as the whole history; the frontier treats names beyond the examined certificates as unexamined.

real_serial_sources._comment: CT sources whose serial is the REAL x509 serial — the only ones cert_pivot turns into a FOFA cert.sn="<decimal>" query (FOFA's cert="<sha256>" matches nothing, live-verified by Quarry 2026-10). CertSpotter (issuance id), CertIndex, Shodan CTL and Censys rows carry a surrogate or no serial and are skipped, so a record backed only by them yields no FOFA query rather than a dead one. The served leaf's own serial (parsed from its DER) always qualifies.
